summary: The article accurately reports on the RBI's repo rate hike in October 2026 and its implications for home loans, with all key factual claims verified by authoritative sources.

claims.claim: On October 7, 2026, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced an increase in the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps), moving it from 5.25% to 5.50%.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the RBI's repo rate hike to 5.50% on October 7, 2026, from 5.25%.

claims.claim: Since October 2019, the RBI mandated that all new floating rate retail loans, including home loans, be linked to an external benchmark.
claims.note: RBI circulars confirm the mandate for linking new floating rate retail loans to external benchmarks from October 1, 2019.

claims.claim: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) typically meets six times a year, bi-monthly, to review the monetary policy, including the repo rate.
claims.note: The RBI Act, 1934, mandates the MPC to meet at least six times a year, bi-monthly.

claims.claim: A basis point (bps) is a common unit of measure in finance, equal to one-hundredth of one percentage point (0.01%). So, a 25 bps hike means an increase of 0.25 percentage points.
claims.note: The definition of a basis point is standard in finance and confirmed by various financial resources.

claims.claim: The current inflation target set by the RBI is 4 percent, with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2 percent.
claims.note: The RBI's inflation target of 4% with a +/- 2% tolerance band is a well-established monetary policy framework.

article_title: RBI Repo Rate Hike: Impact on Your Home Loan EMIs
